bibliographic.title: The Global Majority in International AI Governance
bibliographic.citation_apa: Okolo, C. T., & Raji, M. (2023). The Global Majority in international AI governance. Venue unclear.

methodology.method_family: policy and governance analysis through conceptual lens
methodology.study_design: conceptual book chapter with policy and regulatory landscape review
methodology.sector: international AI governance and development policy
methodology.technology_context: Broad AI governance, national and regional AI strategies, and references to prominent models including ChatGPT, GPT-4, DALL-E, and Claude as examples of Global North dominance

eligibility.decision_rationale: The text is a conceptual chapter on international AI governance and the Global AI Divide, with emphasis on inequities in development, regulation, and participation of Global Majority countries. It references generative AI and models such as ChatGPT and GPT-4 only as illustrations of infrastructure and development asymmetries, and discusses national AI bills, risk-based regulation, and ethical deployment at policy level. It does not address conversational AI systems, operational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, RAG, observability, tracing, human handoff, or post-deployment monitoring of LLM-based conversational systems in regulated environments.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Automated triage scored the item as a central candidate largely due to governance and LLM keyword hits, but full-text review shows no substantive focus on conversational or operational LLM governance.

appraisal.notes: Clear conceptual objective and structured policy-oriented argument, but no empirical sample, no explicit systematic review or data-collection protocol, and limited discussion of study limitations in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The chapter coherently links the Global AI Divide to governance exclusion and policy responses, but its conceptual policy-analysis design offers limited direct evidence for operational conversational LLM governance in regulated settings.

coding.subtheme: Global Majority participation in AI regulation and policy
rq_alignment: background on AI governance in regulated contexts
bias fairness and accountability at policy level
weak alignment to conversational LLM operational governance

synthesis.main_claim: International AI governance is dominated by Western nations and corporations, sidelining Global Majority priorities and perpetuating dependency, while national and regional strategies may offer pathways toward more inclusive governance.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a Global AI Divide lens for analyzing inequities in AI development, innovation, and regulation, and synthesizes emerging policy responses and recommendations for democratizing AI governance.
synthesis.limitations: Conceptual and policy-focused rather than empirical; limited operational detail on AI system deployment controls; generative and conversational AI are referenced peripherally rather than analyzed as governed conversational systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on international and national AI governance, regulation, bias, and risk framing in Global Majority contexts; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance of LLM-based systems.
